{{short description|South Sudanese basketball player (born 2006)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Khaman Maluach | image = Duke at UNC, Mar 2025, Maluach.jpg | image_size = 150px | caption = Maluach with [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] in 2025 | number = | position = [[Center (basketball)|Center]] | height_ft = 7 | height_in = 2 | weight_lbs = 250 | league = | team = | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2006|9|14|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Rumbek]], [[South Sudan]] | high_school = [[NBA Academy Africa]]
([[Saly, Senegal]]) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2024–2025) | career_start = 2022 | years1 = [[2022 BAL season|2022]] | team1 = [[Cobra Sport]] | years2 = [[2023 BAL season|2023]] | team2 = [[AS Douanes (basketball)|AS Douanes]] | years3 = [[2024 BAL season|2024]] | team3 = [[City Oilers]] | highlights = * [[BAL rebounding leader]] ([[2024 BAL season|2024]]) * [[Basketball Without Borders]] MVP (2023) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman Team ([[2024–25 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|2025]]) }} '''Khaman Madit Maluach''' (born 14 September 2006) is a South Sudanese [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. Standing at {{height|ft=7|in=2}}, he plays the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. He is also a current member of the [[South Sudan men's national basketball team|South Sudan national team]], which he joined at the age of 16. ==Early life== Born in [[Rumbek]], [[South Sudan]], Maluach grew up in [[Kawempe]], in neighbouring Uganda, as a refugee with his siblings and mother. He attended Bethel Covenant College in Bwejjaba.{{Cite news |last=Mutebi |first=Charles |date=23 March 2024 |title=Next big thing? The incredible rise of 'City Oilers' Khaman Maluach |url=https://www.newvision.co.ug/category/sports/next-big-thing-the-incredible-rise-of-city-oi-NV_184225 |access-date=19 April 2024 |work=New Vision}} In 2019, Maluach was encouraged to play basketball by a [[boda boda]] motorcyclist who had stopped down when he saw the tall Maluach walking along the road. He attended a local camp organised by [[Luol Deng]] and started playing basketball.{{Citation |title=Khaman Maluach Interview {{!}} NBA Academy Games {{!}} 7.6.23 | date=10 July 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=efck_ZnO-74 |access-date=12 August 2023 |language=en}} He later joined the [[NBA Academy Africa]] in [[Saly, Senegal]], where basketball is combined with education. ==College career== On 6 March 2024, Maluach announced his commitment to [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]]. Ranked as the third-best prospect in the 2025 [[NBA draft]] by ''[[ESPN]]'' at the time, he chose Duke over [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{Cite web |date=6 March 2024 |title=Maluach, top big man in 2024 class, to join Duke |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/39666849/khaman-maluach-top-big-man-2024-class-commits-duke |access-date=15 March 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} He stated that this was due to the impression [[Zion Williamson]] had on him when he was younger.{{Cite web |date=29 September 2024 |title=Duke Prospect Explains Why he Picked the Blue Devils |url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/duke-khaman-maluach-picked-blue-devils-zion-williamson |access-date=30 September 2024 |website=NBA Draft On SI |language=en-US}} ==Professional career== Maluach played for the South Sudanese professional team [[Cobra Sport]] in the [[2022 BAL season]], as part of the BAL Elevate program. Through this programme, one NBA Academy Africa player was assigned to each [[Basketball Africa League]] (BAL) team on an amateur contract.{{Cite web |date=2 March 2022 |title=BAL teams to field one NBA Academy player each in 2022 |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/33403664/nba-launches-bal-elevate-placing-academy-players-teams-tournament |access-date=29 October 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} He made his BAL debut on April 9 against defending champions [[Zamalek SC Basketball|Zamalek]], scoring two points and recording two rebounds in seven minutes.{{Cite web |last=Proballers |title=Khaman Maluach, Basketball Player |url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/252887/khaman-maluach |access-date=29 October 2022 |website=Proballers |language=en}} In March 2023, Maluach played in his second BAL season after he was drafted first among the academy prospects by the [[AS Douanes (basketball)|AS Douanes]], the defending Senegalese champions. The Douanes reached the [[2023 BAL Final|final]], in which Maluach started and contributed 2 points and 4 rebounds, as they lost to [[Al Ahly (basketball)|Al Ahly]].{{Cite web |last=Proballers |title=Khaman Maluach, Basketball Player |url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/252887/khaman-maluach |access-date=12 August 2023 |website=Proballers |language=en}} He attended the 2023 [[Basketball Without Borders]] in [[Johannesburg]], South Africa, and was named the camp's MVP.{{Cite web |title=Egypt's Hassan, Malauch of South Sudan named MVPs of BWB Africa camp |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/egypt-s-hassan-malauch-of-south-sudan-named-mvps-of-bwb-africa-camp |access-date=12 August 2023 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=1 August 2023 |title=South Sudan's Khaman Maluach and Egypt's Aisha Hassan named BWB Africa Most Valuable Players |url=https://ojbsport.com/2023/08/02/south-sudans-khaman-maluach-and-egypts-aisha-hassan-named-bwb-africa-most-valuable-players/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230802005108/https://ojbsport.com/2023/08/02/south-sudans-khaman-maluach-and-egypts-aisha-hassan-named-bwb-africa-most-valuable-players/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=2 August 2023 |access-date=11 August 2023 |website=OJB SPORT |language=en}} On 4 March 2024, it was announced that Maluach was drafted by the Ugandan club [[City Oilers]] for the [[2024 BAL season]].{{Cite web |date=4 March 2024 |title=Top NBA Draft prospects land on new BAL teams |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/39651148/top-nba-draft-prospects-ulrich-chomche-khaman-maluach-land-bal-teams-2024-season |access-date=15 March 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} On 19 April, Maluach had 16 points and 8 rebounds in his Oilers debut in a 76–99 loss to [[Al Ahly (basketball)|Al Ahly]].{{Cite web |title=Al Ahly vs. City Oilers |url=https://fibalivestats.dcd.shared.geniussports.com/u/BAL/2410682/ |access-date=19 April 2024 |website=FIBA Livestats}} One day later, on 20 April, Maluach set new career-highs with 29 points and 11 rebounds in a 88–101 loss against [[Bangui Sporting Club|Bangui]].{{Cite web |date=21 April 2024 |title=How the first Maluach v Darlan duel of the season turned out |url=https://bal.nba.com/news/how-the-first-maluach-v-darlan-duel-of-the-season-turned-out |access-date=23 April 2024 |website=The BAL |language=en}} On 24 April, Maluach had 16 points, 19 rebounds and 7 blocks in a 68–79 loss to [[Al-Ahly Ly SC (basketball)|Al-Ahly Ly]].{{Cite web |title=LiveStats |url=https://geniussports.com/ |access-date=23 April 2024 |website=geniussports.com}} His 19 rebounds set a new career-high, and his 7 blocks set a then league record for most blocks [[List of BAL records|by any player in a BAL game]].{{Cite web |title=Opong says City Oilers can't throw the towel in after dropping to 0-3 |url=https://bal.nba.com/news/opong-says-city-oilers-cant-throw-the-towel-in-after-dropping-to-0-3 |access-date=23 April 2024 |website=The BAL |language=en}} Despite the Oilers being eliminated, Maluach averaged 17.5 points, a league-leading 13.5 rebounds, and 2.8 blocks per game over his six performances.{{Cite web |title=Highlights from the 2024 Nile Conference |url=https://bal.nba.com/news/highlights-from-the-2024-nile-conference |access-date=2 May 2024 |website=The BAL |language=en}} ==National team career== In August 2023, Maluach was selected for the [[South Sudan men's national basketball team|South Sudan national team]] roster for the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. At age 16, he was the youngest player on the Bright Stars' roster.{{Cite web |title=Lakers forward Wenyen Gabriel fortifies South Sudan World Cup squad |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/news/lakers-forward-wenyen-gabriel-fortifies-south-sudan-world-cup-squad |access-date=11 August 2023 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} On 28 August, he made his debut in a victory against [[China men's national basketball team|China]], becoming the third-youngest player to appear in a World Cup game.{{Cite web |title=South Sudan's Khaman Maluach, 16, makes FIBA World Cup debut |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/south-sudans-khaman-maluach-16-makes-fiba-world/story?id=102616871 |access-date=10 September 2023 |website=ABC News |language=en}} Maluach and South Sudan were the best-ranked African team in the tournament, and thus qualified for the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Summer Olympics]] in [[Paris]],
